datasets.name: NASADEM digital elevation model (DEM)
datasets.verbatim: We refer to this mask throughout this paper as the “DEM mask”. Since landslides typically initiate on steep hillslopes, slopes of less than a few degrees can be masked, as these are the areas that generally correspond to non-landslide locations. However, slope thresholds will vary in different regions. Additionally, it is common for landslides to run out into lower-slope areas; therefore it is important to initially consider a wide range of slope values when searching for landslide deposits. We also mask out larger water bodies, including oceans and some lakes and river shorelines, using the water body data stored in the NASADEM layer.

methods.name: SAR backscatter change approach in Google Earth Engine (GEE)
methods.summary: A cloud-based approach in Google Earth Engine that calculates the log ratio of multi-temporal pre-event and post-event SAR backscatter intensity stacks to detect landslides. It incorporates topographic masking (slope and curvature) using NASADEM to reduce false positives and generates landslide density heatmaps using kernel density estimation.
methods.verbatim: Google Earth Engine code for landslide detection in Google Earth Engine is available at https://github.com/alhandwerger/GEE_scripts_for_Handwerger_et_al_2022_NHESS (Handwerger, 2022).
